{
  "schema_version": "formalization-faithfulness-1",
  "role": "blind-translation",
  "dossier_sha256": "1adfed0a19d76d97bab500664cd63018cbb75d3e0a7c94bfad0f67f344344e09",
  "dependency_coverage": [
    {"id":"D001","name":"LocalDef001","meaning":"At every state in the specified set, the flux has a Fréchet derivative whose real matrix has a real eigenbasis.","effect_on_target":"This property is bundled in law and explicitly repeated as a conclusion.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D002","name":"LocalDef002","meaning":"The interval endpoints are strictly increasing, the field is interval integrable, and the specified vector equals its normalized interval integral.","effect_on_target":"Certifies four physical averages and two reference mean fluxes.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D003","name":"LocalDef003","meaning":"The data equals the left state at every negative coordinate and the right state at every positive coordinate; its value at zero is unrestricted.","effect_on_target":"Specifies both reference fields at time zero.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D004","name":"LocalDef004","meaning":"By D026, a law packages positive dimension, a set of states, a globally defined flux, and D001 on that set.","effect_on_target":"Restricts the quantified laws and supplies the state set and flux.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D005","name":"LocalDef005","meaning":"Projects the law's flux, a function from real m-vectors to real m-vectors.","effect_on_target":"Used in physical balance, reference balance, and flux averages.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D006","name":"LocalDef006","meaning":"Projects the law's specified set of states.","effect_on_target":"Restricts the three input states and the reference fields at positive times.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D007","name":"LocalDef007","meaning":"By D010, a problem packages two states in the law's state set and a strictly positive real duration.","effect_on_target":"Indexes results, accuracy bounds, admission, and reference objects.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D008","name":"LocalDef008","meaning":"Projects a problem's duration.","effect_on_target":"Both constructed problems have duration t-s, also used to average reference flux.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D009","name":"LocalDef009","meaning":"Projects a problem's left state.","effect_on_target":"Identifies the left states of the two problems and their reference initial data.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D010","name":"LocalDef010","meaning":"Constructs a problem from two states, their membership proofs, a duration, and its positivity proof.","effect_on_target":"Constructs the left-center and center-right problems with duration t-s.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D011","name":"LocalDef011","meaning":"Projects a problem's right state.","effect_on_target":"Identifies the right states of the two problems and their reference initial data.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D012","name":"LocalDef012","meaning":"By D027, a reference object packages a space-time field with the problem's step initial data, positive-time state membership, spatial and temporal integrability, and integral balance on its time strip.","effect_on_target":"The accuracy assumption and final conclusion quantify over these constrained reference objects.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D013","name":"LocalDef013","meaning":"Projects a reference object's field, with spatial coordinate first and time second.","effect_on_target":"Provides reference initial data, balance integrands, and the trace at spatial zero.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D014","name":"LocalDef014","meaning":"The normalized integral of the reference flux at spatial zero over times from zero to the problem duration.","effect_on_target":"Defines the comparison flux in accuracy and the final error estimate.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D015","name":"LocalDef015","meaning":"By D028, a routine packages an admission predicate, an admitted-problem solver, an information extractor, and an information-to-vector numerical flux function.","effect_on_target":"Provides an abstract computational pipeline without additional correctness conditions beyond the separate accuracy assumption.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D016","name":"LocalDef016","meaning":"For every problem and proof of admission, some reference object has mean flux within errorBound(problem) of the routine flux in the finite-product norm.","effect_on_target":"Assumed globally on the routine's domain; supplies the two reference witnesses and their error bounds.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D017","name":"LocalDef017","meaning":"Projects the routine's problem-admission predicate.","effect_on_target":"Both constructed problems must satisfy it; it need not hold for every problem.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D018","name":"LocalDef018","meaning":"Projects the function extracting Information from a result indexed by its problem.","effect_on_target":"Forms the middle stage of each numerical flux computation.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D019","name":"LocalDef019","meaning":"Solves an admitted problem, extracts information, and applies numericalFlux.","effect_on_target":"Defines leftFlux and rightFlux and explains the two pipeline equalities.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D020","name":"LocalDef020","meaning":"Projects the function from Information to a real m-vector.","effect_on_target":"Produces the numerical flux after extraction.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D021","name":"LocalDef021","meaning":"Projects the function returning a problem-indexed result for each admitted problem.","effect_on_target":"Provides the solver stage; admission is required.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D022","name":"LocalDef022","meaning":"Multiplies the integral over a region by the inverse of the real conversion of that region's measure.","effect_on_target":"The old spatial average is identified with this average for Lebesgue measure on (a,b].","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D023","name":"LocalDef023","meaning":"Returns oldAverage minus (timeStep/cellVolume) times netOutwardFlux.","effect_on_target":"Defines next using center and rightFlux-leftFlux.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D024","name":"LocalDef024","meaning":"The interval integral multiplied by the inverse of right-left.","effect_on_target":"Defines all spatial and temporal averages in the statement.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D025","name":"LocalDef025","meaning":"There exists a continuous real-linear derivative of the flux at the state whose coordinate matrix satisfies D031.","effect_on_target":"Requires ambient Fréchet differentiability and real diagonalizability at every admitted state.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D026","name":"LocalDef026","meaning":"Constructs a law from 0<m, a state set, a flux, and the pointwise derivative/eigenbasis property on that set.","effect_on_target":"Exposes the assumptions implicit in the law binder.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D027","name":"LocalDef027","meaning":"Constructs a reference from a field satisfying step initial data; state membership for every x and 0<τ≤duration; spatial interval integrability for every pair of endpoints at 0≤τ≤duration; flux-trace interval integrability for every x and 0≤u≤v≤duration; and integral balance for all spatial endpoints and such times.","effect_on_target":"Makes reference witnesses carry these conditions, including conditions not separately restated in the final conjunction.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D028","name":"LocalDef028","meaning":"Constructs a routine from its domain, dependent solver, extractor, and numerical flux function.","effect_on_target":"Confirms that no other solver or flux properties are bundled.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D029","name":"LocalDef029","meaning":"The identity ring homomorphism on the reals forms an inverse pair with itself.","effect_on_target":"Supports ordinary real-linear equivalences used in matrix conversion.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D030","name":"LocalDef030","meaning":"The two real scalar actions on real m-vectors commute.","effect_on_target":"Supports the real module structure on spaces of linear maps.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D031","name":"LocalDef031","meaning":"There exist real eigenvalues indexed by the matrix index type and a real basis of its vector space such that each basis vector is an eigenvector with the corresponding eigenvalue.","effect_on_target":"Requires a full real eigenbasis, with no distinctness or ordering requirement on eigenvalues.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D032","name":"AddGroup.toSubNegMonoid","meaning":"Forgets an additive group to its addition, negation, and subtraction structure.","effect_on_target":"Supplies ordinary real subtraction in duration positivity.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D033","name":"AddGroup.toSubtractionMonoid","meaning":"Derives subtraction and negation identities from an additive group.","effect_on_target":"Supports the real arithmetic instances used in the problem constructors.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D034","name":"AddMonoid.toAddZeroClass","meaning":"Retains addition, zero, and the zero identity laws from an additive monoid.","effect_on_target":"Supplies the usual additive zero in real arithmetic.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D035","name":"AddRightCancelSemigroup.toIsRightCancelAdd","meaning":"Addition in an additive right-cancellative semigroup is right cancellative.","effect_on_target":"Supports strict order preservation used to prove t-s>0.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D036","name":"AddZero.toAdd","meaning":"Projects addition from a structure carrying addition and zero.","effect_on_target":"Selects real addition in the order-instance chain.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D037","name":"AddZeroClass.toAddZero","meaning":"Forgets zero identity laws while retaining addition and zero.","effect_on_target":"Supplies the same real arithmetic operations.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D038","name":"Algebra.id","meaning":"A commutative semiring is an algebra over itself via the identity map, with scalar action given by multiplication.","effect_on_target":"Makes real scalar multiplication of real coordinates ordinary multiplication.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D039","name":"Algebra.toSMul","meaning":"Projects the scalar action of an algebra.","effect_on_target":"Supplies real scalar multiplication in vector update and balance expressions.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D040","name":"And","meaning":"Logical conjunction.","effect_on_target":"All listed conclusions must hold together.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D041","name":"CommSemiring.toSemiring","meaning":"Forgets multiplication commutativity from a commutative semiring.","effect_on_target":"Supplies underlying real semiring operations without a new assumption.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D042","name":"DivInvMonoid.toDiv","meaning":"Projects division from the division-and-inverse structure.","effect_on_target":"Selects real division in the positive time-to-width ratio.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D043","name":"Eq","meaning":"Equality of two objects of the same type.","effect_on_target":"Vector equalities are exact and hence hold in every coordinate.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D044","name":"Exists","meaning":"Existential quantification over the specified type.","effect_on_target":"The two reference objects exist; they are not universally prescribed or claimed unique.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D045","name":"Fin","meaning":"The finite index type of natural numbers strictly below m.","effect_on_target":"States are functions on indices 0 through m-1.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D046","name":"Fin.fintype","meaning":"Enumerates all indices in Fin n.","effect_on_target":"Supports finite-product norms, finite-dimensional vector spaces, and matrix sums.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D047","name":"Function.hasSMul","meaning":"Lifts scalar multiplication pointwise to function spaces.","effect_on_target":"Scalar-vector products act independently in each coordinate.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D048","name":"HAdd.hAdd","meaning":"Applies the selected addition operation.","effect_on_target":"Adds real bounds and adds vectors componentwise.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D049","name":"HDiv.hDiv","meaning":"Applies the selected division operation.","effect_on_target":"Forms (t-s)/(b-a).","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D050","name":"HMul.hMul","meaning":"Applies the selected multiplication operation.","effect_on_target":"Multiplies real error sums by the time-to-width ratio.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D051","name":"HSMul.hSMul","meaning":"Applies the selected scalar multiplication operation.","effect_on_target":"Scales vector integrals, flux differences, and errors by real numbers.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D052","name":"HSub.hSub","meaning":"Applies the selected subtraction operation.","effect_on_target":"Forms endpoint differences and signed vector errors.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D053","name":"Iff.mpr","meaning":"From P if and only if Q and a proof of Q, derives P.","effect_on_target":"Uses s<t to supply the constructor proof 0<t-s.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D054","name":"InnerProductSpace.toNormedSpace","meaning":"Retains the norm-compatible scalar module from an inner product space.","effect_on_target":"Supplies the real coordinate normed space used in vector integration.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D055","name":"IntervalIntegrable","meaning":"Integrability on both (a,b] and (b,a] with respect to the stated measure.","effect_on_target":"For increasing endpoints, requires integrability on the forward interval; also handles reversed spatial endpoints in reference conditions.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D056","name":"IsOrderedAddMonoid.toAddLeftMono","meaning":"Left addition preserves non-strict order in an ordered additive commutative monoid.","effect_on_target":"Supports the positivity proof for the duration.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D057","name":"IsRightCancelAdd.addRightStrictMono_of_addRightMono","meaning":"Right-cancellative, order-preserving right addition in a partial order also preserves strict order.","effect_on_target":"Supports the subtraction positivity equivalence.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D058","name":"LE.le","meaning":"Applies the selected non-strict order relation.","effect_on_target":"Expresses real error bounds and closed time-strip restrictions.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D059","name":"LT.lt","meaning":"Applies the selected strict order relation.","effect_on_target":"Expresses positive dimension, positive lengths, and the two open initial-data half-lines.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D060","name":"MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace","meaning":"Projects the measurable space underlying a measure space.","effect_on_target":"Provides the measurable structure for the real interval region average.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D061","name":"MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume","meaning":"Projects the distinguished measure of a measure space.","effect_on_target":"All target integrals use the distinguished real volume measure.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D062","name":"Membership.mem","meaning":"Applies the selected membership relation, with the set argument before the element.","effect_on_target":"Requires left, center, and right to belong to law.states.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D063","name":"Nat","meaning":"The natural numbers including zero.","effect_on_target":"Indexes vector dimension, with zero excluded by the law structure.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D064","name":"NegZeroClass.toZero","meaning":"Projects zero from a negation-and-zero structure.","effect_on_target":"Supplies the real zero in positivity proofs.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D065","name":"NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring.toAddCommMonoid","meaning":"Retains the additive commutative monoid of a semiring-like structure.","effect_on_target":"Supplies real additive operations for the pointwise vector module.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D066","name":"NonUnitalSeminormedCommRing.toNonUnitalSeminormedRing","meaning":"Forgets multiplication commutativity from a nonunital seminormed ring.","effect_on_target":"Preserves the real norm and operations used to construct vector normed spaces.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D067","name":"NonUnitalSeminormedRing.toSeminormedAddCommGroup","meaning":"Retains a ring's additive group, norm, and compatible pseudometric.","effect_on_target":"Supplies the additive normed structure needed by integration and scalar multiplication.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D068","name":"NonUnitalSemiring.toNonUnitalNonAssocSemiring","meaning":"Forgets multiplication associativity from a nonunital semiring.","effect_on_target":"Part of the real module instance chain; does not alter operations.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D069","name":"Norm.norm","meaning":"Projects the real-valued norm function.","effect_on_target":"Measures each vector error with the chosen finite-product norm.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D070","name":"NormedAddCommGroup.toNormedAddGroup","meaning":"Retains a normed additive group while forgetting commutativity.","effect_on_target":"Supplies the norm structure for interval integrability.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D071","name":"NormedAddGroup.toENormedAddMonoid","meaning":"Provides the associated extended nonnegative norm and additive monoid from a normed additive group.","effect_on_target":"Interprets integrability using the same underlying vector norm.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D072","name":"NormedCommRing.toNormedRing","meaning":"Forgets multiplication commutativity from a normed ring.","effect_on_target":"Supplies real coordinate norms in the finite-product normed ring.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D073","name":"NormedCommRing.toSeminormedCommRing","meaning":"Retains the norm, commutative ring operations, and pseudometric while forgetting metric separation.","effect_on_target":"Preserves the real analytic structure in vector-space construction.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D074","name":"NormedRing.toNorm","meaning":"Projects a normed ring's norm.","effect_on_target":"Selects the product norm for the error inequalities.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D075","name":"NormedSpace.toModule","meaning":"Projects the underlying scalar module of a normed space.","effect_on_target":"Supplies scalar multiplication for the algebraic update.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D076","name":"OfNat.ofNat","meaning":"Interprets a natural numeral in the selected type.","effect_on_target":"Interprets the zeros in dimension, time, and error conditions.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D077","name":"PartialOrder.toPreorder","meaning":"Retains reflexive and transitive order from a partial order.","effect_on_target":"Supplies ordinary real interval and inequality structure.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D078","name":"Pi.Function.module","meaning":"The pointwise module structure on functions into a module.","effect_on_target":"Makes real m-vectors a real vector space for the update.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D079","name":"Pi.addCommGroup","meaning":"The componentwise additive commutative group on a function space.","effect_on_target":"Gives vector addition and subtraction in the update.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D080","name":"Pi.instAdd","meaning":"Function addition is defined by (f+g)(i)=f(i)+g(i).","effect_on_target":"Vector sums in the balance and error identities are componentwise.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D081","name":"Pi.instSub","meaning":"Function subtraction is defined by (f-g)(i)=f(i)-g(i).","effect_on_target":"Flux differences and errors are componentwise differences.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D082","name":"Pi.normedAddCommGroup","meaning":"The finite-product normed additive commutative group inherited from Pi.seminormedAddGroup.","effect_on_target":"Provides the finite-product norm and metric for vector integrals.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D083","name":"Pi.normedAddGroup","meaning":"The finite-product normed additive group inherited from Pi.seminormedAddGroup.","effect_on_target":"Provides the vector norm underlying interval integrability.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D084","name":"Pi.normedRing","meaning":"The finite-product normed ring, with norm inherited from Pi.seminormedRing and pointwise ring operations.","effect_on_target":"Selects the standard finite-product maximum norm for error bounds, rather than a sum of coordinate errors.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D085","name":"Pi.normedSpace","meaning":"The pointwise scalar module on a finite product, compatible with its product norm.","effect_on_target":"Supports vector integration and norm estimates under real scaling.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D086","name":"Pi.topologicalSpace","meaning":"The product topology induced by all coordinate evaluations.","effect_on_target":"The vector fields use the ordinary finite-dimensional product topology.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D087","name":"Preorder.toLE","meaning":"Projects non-strict comparison from a preorder.","effect_on_target":"Supplies real ≤ in order-instance construction.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D088","name":"PseudoMetricSpace.toUniformSpace","meaning":"Projects the uniform structure associated with a pseudometric.","effect_on_target":"Links the usual real metric to the topology used in integrability.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D089","name":"RCLike.toInnerProductSpaceReal","meaning":"Provides the standard real inner product space structure on a real- or complex-like scalar field.","effect_on_target":"Here it supplies the ordinary one-dimensional real normed space on each coordinate.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D090","name":"Real","meaning":"The real numbers.","effect_on_target":"Coordinates, space, time, flux components, and bounds are real-valued.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D091","name":"Real.instAdd","meaning":"Ordinary real addition.","effect_on_target":"Adds bounds and endpoint arithmetic expressions.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D092","name":"Real.instAddCommGroup","meaning":"The usual additive commutative group of real numbers.","effect_on_target":"Supplies coordinatewise vector group operations.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D093","name":"Real.instAddCommMonoid","meaning":"The usual real additive commutative monoid.","effect_on_target":"Supports order compatibility of real addition.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D094","name":"Real.instAddCommSemigroup","meaning":"Associative and commutative real addition.","effect_on_target":"Permits transferring order preservation between left and right addition.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D095","name":"Real.instAddGroup","meaning":"The usual real additive group.","effect_on_target":"Supports subtraction and duration positivity.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D096","name":"Real.instAddRightCancelSemigroup","meaning":"The right-cancellative additive structure of the reals.","effect_on_target":"Supports strict monotonicity in the duration positivity proof.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D097","name":"Real.instCommSemiring","meaning":"The usual commutative semiring structure on the reals.","effect_on_target":"Supports multiplication-based real scalar actions.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D098","name":"Real.instDivInvMonoid","meaning":"Real division is multiplication by the real inverse.","effect_on_target":"Determines the time-to-width quotient.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D099","name":"Real.instIsOrderedAddMonoid","meaning":"Real addition preserves non-strict order.","effect_on_target":"Supports proving t-s>0 from s<t.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D100","name":"Real.instLE","meaning":"Ordinary real non-strict order.","effect_on_target":"Interprets all real upper bounds and nonnegative-time conditions.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D101","name":"Real.instLT","meaning":"Ordinary real strict order.","effect_on_target":"Interprets increasing endpoints, positive duration, and initial half-lines.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D102","name":"Real.instMul","meaning":"Ordinary real multiplication.","effect_on_target":"Weights scalar error bounds and coordinate scalar products.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D103","name":"Real.instPreorder","meaning":"The usual real preorder.","effect_on_target":"Defines interval membership and non-strict comparisons.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D104","name":"Real.instRCLike","meaning":"The reals as a complete real-like normed field, with real part the identity and imaginary part zero.","effect_on_target":"Supplies standard real analytic and inner product instances; introduces no complex coordinates.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D105","name":"Real.instRing","meaning":"The usual ring structure of the reals.","effect_on_target":"Supplies algebraic operations for the real vector module.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D106","name":"Real.instSub","meaning":"Real subtraction a-b is a+(-b).","effect_on_target":"Fixes the signs of durations, widths, and componentwise errors.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D107","name":"Real.instZero","meaning":"The real number zero.","effect_on_target":"Specifies the reference interface, initial time, and nonnegative bounds.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D108","name":"Real.measureSpace","meaning":"The standard measure-space structure on the reals.","effect_on_target":"Its volume is the Lebesgue measure used in all averages and balances.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D109","name":"Real.normedAddCommGroup","meaning":"The usual real additive group with absolute-value norm and standard metric.","effect_on_target":"Provides the coordinate norm and integral codomain structure.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D110","name":"Real.normedCommRing","meaning":"The real commutative ring with its absolute-value norm.","effect_on_target":"Supplies the coordinate norms used by the product normed ring.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D111","name":"Real.normedField","meaning":"The real field with absolute-value norm and totalized inverse, including inverse zero equal to zero.","effect_on_target":"Supports real normed vector spaces and averaging denominators, which are positive here.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D112","name":"Real.partialOrder","meaning":"The usual antisymmetric real order with its associated strict order.","effect_on_target":"Supports the inequalities and duration positivity derivation.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D113","name":"Real.pseudoMetricSpace","meaning":"The distance between real numbers x and y is |x-y|.","effect_on_target":"Fixes the standard topology used for vector-field integrability.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D114","name":"Real.semiring","meaning":"The usual real semiring structure.","effect_on_target":"Supplies scalar algebra in the update module.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D115","name":"Ring.toSemiring","meaning":"Retains semiring operations from a ring.","effect_on_target":"Preserves ordinary real addition and multiplication in module construction.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D116","name":"SeminormedCommRing.toNonUnitalSeminormedCommRing","meaning":"Forgets the unit requirement while retaining the seminormed commutative ring operations and metric.","effect_on_target":"Part of the coordinate analytic instance chain; adds no restriction.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D117","name":"Semiring.toNonUnitalSemiring","meaning":"Forgets the unit from a semiring.","effect_on_target":"Supplies the same real additive structure needed for a module.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D118","name":"Set","meaning":"A set of elements of a type is a predicate on that type.","effect_on_target":"law.states can be any predicate satisfying the bundled derivative requirement.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D119","name":"Set.Ioc","meaning":"The half-open interval {x : a<x and x≤b}.","effect_on_target":"Fixes the region in the set-average equality and interval integral definitions.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D120","name":"Set.instMembership","meaning":"Set membership evaluates the set's predicate.","effect_on_target":"Interprets admissibility of states and interval regions.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D121","name":"SubNegMonoid.toAddMonoid","meaning":"Projects the additive monoid from a subtraction-and-negation structure.","effect_on_target":"Supports ordinary real addition in positivity proofs.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D122","name":"SubNegMonoid.toSub","meaning":"Projects subtraction from a subtraction-and-negation structure.","effect_on_target":"Supplies t-s in the proof of positive duration.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D123","name":"SubNegZeroMonoid.toNegZeroClass","meaning":"Retains zero, negation, and negation of zero equal to zero.","effect_on_target":"Supplies the real zero used in constructor positivity.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D124","name":"SubtractionMonoid.toSubNegZeroMonoid","meaning":"Derives negation preserving zero from subtraction-monoid identities.","effect_on_target":"Supports the zero-instance chain without changing numerical values.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D125","name":"UniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace","meaning":"Projects the topology of a uniform space.","effect_on_target":"Provides the usual real topology and hence the vector product topology.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D126","name":"Zero.toOfNat0","meaning":"Interprets the numeral 0 as the selected zero element.","effect_on_target":"All displayed real zeros denote the ordinary real zero.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D127","name":"covariant_swap_add_of_covariant_add","meaning":"For commutative addition, preservation of a relation by left addition implies preservation by right addition.","effect_on_target":"Supports the order argument establishing positive duration.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D128","name":"instHAdd","meaning":"Uses homogeneous addition as heterogeneous addition on the same type.","effect_on_target":"Resolves real and vector additions to their ordinary operations.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D129","name":"instHDiv","meaning":"Uses homogeneous division as heterogeneous division on the same type.","effect_on_target":"Resolves the real quotient in the update and estimates.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D130","name":"instHMul","meaning":"Uses homogeneous multiplication as heterogeneous multiplication on the same type.","effect_on_target":"Resolves multiplication of real bounds and ratios.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D131","name":"instHSMul","meaning":"Uses an ordinary scalar action as heterogeneous scalar multiplication.","effect_on_target":"Resolves real scaling of vectors.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D132","name":"instHSub","meaning":"Uses homogeneous subtraction as heterogeneous subtraction on the same type.","effect_on_target":"Resolves real differences and pointwise vector differences.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D133","name":"instLTNat","meaning":"The usual strict order on natural numbers.","effect_on_target":"The dimension conclusion means m is at least one.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D134","name":"instOfNatNat","meaning":"Interprets a natural-number numeral as itself.","effect_on_target":"The zero in 0<m is natural zero.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D135","name":"intervalIntegral","meaning":"The integral over (a,b] minus the integral over (b,a], with the specified measure.","effect_on_target":"All interval integrals are oriented; reference spatial endpoints need not be ordered.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D136","name":"sub_pos","meaning":"In the indicated ordered additive group, 0<a-b if and only if b<a.","effect_on_target":"Constructs positive durations from s<t.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D137","name":"AddCommGroup","meaning":"An abelian group written additively.","effect_on_target":"Provides the generic algebraic setting of the update, instantiated by real m-vectors.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D138","name":"AddCommGroup.toAddCommMonoid","meaning":"Forgets additive inverses while retaining commutative addition and zero.","effect_on_target":"Supplies module and scalar-action prerequisites.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D139","name":"AddCommGroup.toAddGroup","meaning":"Forgets commutativity from an additive commutative group.","effect_on_target":"Supplies additive-group operations for dependent constructions.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D140","name":"AddZero.toZero","meaning":"Projects zero from a structure with addition and zero.","effect_on_target":"Provides vector or scalar zero through inherited algebraic structures.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D141","name":"DFunLike.coe","meaning":"Evaluates an object through its underlying dependent function.","effect_on_target":"Enables application of bundled maps and measures without changing their mathematical action.","status":"understood"},
    {"id":"D142","name":"DistribMulAction.toDistribSMul","meaning":"Retains scalar multiplication distributing over addition and preserving zero.","effect_on_target":"Supports scalar multiplication used in normalized integrals.","status":"understood"},

  "translation": {
    "binders": [
      "Universally quantify a natural number m and a law on V = (Fin m → R), identified with real m-vectors. The law packages m>0, a state set S⊆V, a globally defined flux F:V→V, and the derivative/eigenbasis condition described below.",
      "Universally quantify an arbitrary problem-indexed family of types Result(P), an arbitrary type Information, a routine with these types, and an arbitrary real-valued function e(P)=errorBound(P) on all problems. The type universes u_1 and u_2 are arbitrary.",
      "A problem P consists of two vectors in S and a positive duration. The routine consists of D(P):Prop, solve(P,h):Result(P) for each h:D(P), extract:Result(P)→Information for every P, and numericalFlux:Information→V.",
      "Universally quantify left, center, right∈V and proofs that all three belong to S; real numbers a,b,s,t with a<b and s<t; and proofs admitting the two constructed problems P_L=(left,center,t-s) and P_R=(center,right,t-s) to D.",
      "Universally quantify q:R→R→V, with spatial coordinate first and time second.",
      "Within one conclusion, universally quantify real numbers oldBound, leftBound, rightBound, followed by the three stated norm-bound hypotheses.",
      "Existentially quantify L:LocalDef012(P_L), then R:LocalDef012(P_R). Both witnesses are chosen after the outer data and hypotheses and before the final universal bounds. Their types depend on their respective problems. R may be chosen after L, but its type does not depend on L.",
      "For each reference's balance conclusion, universally quantify arbitrary real spatial endpoints x,y and real times u,v satisfying 0≤u≤v≤t-s.",
      "Inside the existential reference conclusion, universally quantify real numbers oldBound, leftComparison, rightComparison, followed by the three stated comparison hypotheses. The chosen references must work for every such triple."
    ],
    "hypotheses": [
      "The law's bundled condition is: for every z∈S, F has a continuous real-linear Fréchet derivative A_z at z in the full ambient space V, and there exist real numbers λ_i and a real basis (v_i) indexed by Fin m such that the coordinate matrix of A_z satisfies A_z v_i=λ_i v_i for every i.",
      "The routine satisfies the following accuracy property: for every problem P and every admission proof h:D(P), there exists a reference W for P with ||numericalFlux(extract(solve(P,h)))-M(W)||≤e(P), where M(W) is the mean flux at spatial zero over the problem's duration.",
      "left, center, and right belong to S; a<b and s<t; D(P_L) and D(P_R) hold.",
      "The functions x↦q(x,s) and x↦q(x,t) are interval integrable from a to b with respect to Lebesgue measure.",
      "The functions τ↦F(q(a,τ)) and τ↦F(q(b,τ)) are interval integrable from s to t with respect to Lebesgue measure.",
      "The specified physical balance holds exactly: ∫_a^b q(x,t) dx - ∫_a^b q(x,s) dx = ∫_s^t [F(q(a,τ))-F(q(b,τ))] dτ."
    ],
    "conclusions": [
      "All following assertions hold jointly, with Δx=b-a>0, Δt=t-s>0, ν=Δt/Δx, P_L=(left,center,Δt), P_R=(center,right,Δt), G_L=routine.flux(P_L,hleftDomain), G_R=routine.flux(P_R,hrightDomain), and N=center-ν(G_R-G_L).",
      "m>0, and for every z∈S the flux is Fréchet differentiable at z with a derivative admitting a real eigenbasis.",
      "P_L.left=left, P_L.right=center, P_R.left=center, and P_R.right=right.",
      "P_L.duration=Δt and P_R.duration=Δt.",
      "G_L=numericalFlux(extract(solve(P_L,hleftDomain))) and G_R=numericalFlux(extract(solve(P_R,hrightDomain))).",
      "Writing Q_s=(1/Δx)∫_a^b q(x,s) dx and Q_t=(1/Δx)∫_a^b q(x,t) dx, both are certified interval averages: a<b, the respective field is interval integrable, and the proposed average equals the normalized interval integral.",
      "Writing H_a=(1/Δt)∫_s^t F(q(a,τ)) dτ and H_b=(1/Δt)∫_s^t F(q(b,τ)) dτ, both are certified interval averages: s<t, the respective trace is interval integrable, and the proposed average equals the normalized interval integral.",
      "Q_s also equals the region average (volume((a,b]).toReal)^(-1) times ∫_(a,b] q(x,s) dx.",
      "The defined next vector satisfies N=center-(Δt/Δx)(G_R-G_L).",
      "The exact error identity is Δx(N-Q_t)=Δx(center-Q_s)+Δt[(G_L-H_a)-(G_R-H_b)].",
      "For every oldBound,leftBound,rightBound∈R, if ||center-Q_s||≤oldBound, ||G_L-H_a||≤leftBound, and ||G_R-H_b||≤rightBound, then ||N-Q_t||≤oldBound+ν(leftBound+rightBound).",
      "There exist reference objects L for P_L and R for P_R. Their fields satisfy L(x,0)=left for x<0 and L(x,0)=center for x>0, and R(x,0)=center for x<0 and R(x,0)=right for x>0.",
      "For each W∈{L,R}, every x,y∈R, and every 0≤u≤v≤Δt, the exact balance holds: ∫_x^y W(z,v) dz-∫_x^y W(z,u) dz=∫_u^v [F(W(x,τ))-F(W(y,τ))] dτ.",
      "For these same references, M_L=(1/Δt)∫_0^Δt F(L(0,τ)) dτ and M_R=(1/Δt)∫_0^Δt F(R(0,τ)) dτ are certified interval averages of their respective traces on [0,Δt]: the endpoints are strictly ordered, the traces are interval integrable, and these equalities hold.",
      "e(P_L)≥0, e(P_R)≥0, ||G_L-M_L||≤e(P_L), and ||G_R-M_R||≤e(P_R).",
      "For these fixed references and every oldBound,leftComparison,rightComparison∈R, if ||center-Q_s||≤oldBound, ||M_L-H_a||≤leftComparison, and ||M_R-H_b||≤rightComparison, then ||N-Q_t||≤oldBound+ν[(e(P_L)+leftComparison)+(e(P_R)+rightComparison)].",
      "As part of their reference types, both L and R also take values in S for every spatial coordinate and every 0<τ≤Δt; have spatially interval-integrable slices on every finite interval at each 0≤τ≤Δt; and have interval-integrable flux traces at every spatial coordinate on every 0≤u≤v≤Δt."
    ],
    "mathematical_definitions": [
      "V is the real vector space of functions on Fin m={0,...,m-1}. Addition, subtraction, and real scalar multiplication are coordinatewise. The selected norm is the standard finite-product norm, ||v||=max_i |v_i| for the positive dimensions allowed by law.",
      "All integrals are vector-valued Bochner integrals with real Lebesgue measure. The oriented integral ∫_c^d f is defined as the integral over (c,d] minus the integral over (d,c].",
      "Interval integrability from c to d means integrability on both (c,d] and (d,c].",
      "For a vector field f:R→V, A(f;c,d)=(d-c)^(-1)∫_c^d f. A certified interval average v requires c<d, interval integrability, and v=A(f;c,d).",
      "The region average for measure μ and set E is (μ(E).toReal)^(-1) times the integral of the field with respect to μ restricted to E.",
      "A law requires a positive dimension and pointwise real diagonalizability of the ambient flux derivative throughout its state set. Eigenvalues may repeat; the basis and eigenvalues may depend on the state.",
      "A reference for a problem (l,r,T) is a globally defined field W:R×R→V whose time-zero data is l on x<0 and r on x>0, whose values belong to S for 0<τ≤T, whose spatial slices are integrable on every finite interval for 0≤τ≤T, whose flux traces are integrable on every time subinterval 0≤u≤v≤T, and which satisfies the integral balance on all such rectangles.",
      "A reference mean flux is M(W)=A(τ↦F(W(0,τ));0,T). It is evaluated at the reference interface x=0 and reference times starting at zero.",
      "The routine flux is the composition numericalFlux∘extract∘solve, evaluated on an admitted problem.",
      "The update is oldAverage-(timeStep/cellVolume)netOutwardFlux; here oldAverage=center, timeStep=Δt, cellVolume=Δx, and netOutwardFlux=G_R-G_L."
    ],
    "proposition_plain_english": "For every positive-dimensional real-vector law whose flux derivative admits a real eigenbasis at each specified state, and every abstract admitted-problem routine whose numerical flux is within a prescribed problem-dependent error of some integral-balance reference mean flux, take three specified states, a positive spatial interval, a positive time interval, and admission of the adjacent left-center and center-right problems for that duration. For any field q with the four required integrable slices and boundary flux traces satisfying the stated balance on that single rectangle, the numerical update from the center state satisfies an exact identity relating its new spatial-average error to the old spatial-average error and the two numerical-versus-physical boundary-flux errors. Consequently, every set of upper bounds on those three errors gives the stated one-step norm bound. Moreover, there exist two reference fields for the adjacent problems, with their full bundled state, integrability, initial-data, and balance properties, whose mean fluxes meet the routine's accuracy bounds. For these fixed references, every upper bound on the old error and the two reference-versus-physical mean-flux differences yields the final bound with the two routine accuracy errors added. The proposition also jointly records positive dimension, the law's derivative property, the constructed problem components, the numerical-flux pipeline equalities, and the average certifications."
  },
  "restrictions_and_vacuity_risks": [
    "A law cannot be supplied at m=0 because its constructor requires m>0; the positive-dimension conclusion repeats a bundled restriction.",
    "The state set is not required to be nonempty, open, convex, or invariant under the numerical update. If it is empty, no triple of state-membership hypotheses can be supplied.",
    "The routine domain is an arbitrary predicate and can be empty. The accuracy assumption is vacuous on an empty domain, and the target requires admission of both particular problems before giving its conclusions.",
    "The accuracy property is existential in the reference separately for every admitted problem. It does not compare against every reference, assert uniqueness, or specify a common canonical reference selection.",
    "The error function is arbitrary outside the routine domain. Nonnegativity is a consequence of the norm bounds on admitted problems, not an independently imposed global requirement.",
    "a<b and s<t exclude zero and reversed cell lengths and durations. No upper bound on Δt/Δx, wave speed condition, or CFL condition is imposed.",
    "The physical field q is not required to take values in S, satisfy the conservation equation pointwise, satisfy balance on every rectangle, or possess any regularity beyond the four stated integrability conditions and one balance equality.",
    "The center state need not equal the old spatial average Q_s. The left and right states need not be averages or traces of q. Their relationship to q enters only through error and comparison bounds.",
    "Neither the average Q_t nor the updated state N is asserted to belong to S.",
    "Reference initial data has no requirement at spatial zero. Reference state membership is imposed only for strictly positive times up to the duration, so even W(0,0) need not lie in S.",
    "Reference fields are globally defined, but their membership, integrability, and balance requirements concern only times in [0,Δt]. Their values outside this strip are unconstrained by the reference constructor.",
    "Reference balance is required for every pair of spatial endpoints, including reversed or equal endpoints, using oriented integrals. Its temporal endpoints satisfy 0≤u≤v≤Δt and may coincide.",
    "No entropy inequality, admissibility selection among weak reference fields, self-similarity, finite propagation, or uniqueness of reference fields is encoded.",
    "The derivative requirement is ambient Fréchet differentiability at states in S, with real diagonalizability. It does not require distinct eigenvalues, a uniform eigenbasis bound, continuous eigenvalue or eigenbasis selection, or differentiability at points outside S.",
    "Reference mean fluxes use spatial zero and times [0,Δt]; physical boundary means use spatial a or b and times [s,t]. No translation or equality linking the reference fields to q is assumed. The final comparison hypotheses explicitly bound these differences.",
    "The real numbers used as proposed upper bounds have no independent nonnegativity assumptions. Their antecedent norm inequalities imply nonnegativity when satisfied; with an impossible proposed bound, the associated conditional estimate is vacuous.",
    "The result concerns one algebraic update and conditional error bounds. It does not assert iteration, convergence, a rate under mesh refinement, or existence of suitable small comparison bounds.",
    "All averages used substantively here have positive finite interval lengths and explicit or bundled integrability. Thus general totalization issues for inverses, measure conversion, or integrals outside their usual domains do not supply a degeneracy in these applications."
  ],
